findings.detail: Before this change a 429 `limit: 0` was not `isModelUnavailable`, so it fell into the `isKeyIssue` branch and called `rotateKey()` — a user with two keys configured would move to key B, whose project may well have quota. Now `classifyModelFailure` returns `no-quota`, `advanceModel` walks the candidate list on key A, and when the list is exhausted it *throws* from inside the catch, so `rotateKey()` is never reached. Concrete failure: a user pastes a dud/unbilled key first and a working one second; Translator (and Compare / Support Chat, same shape at :638 and :673) now fails with "No usable Gemini model…" after one request per candidate instead of succeeding on key 2. The common case is improved — falling to Flash on the same key is far better than four 60s waits — which is why this is medium and not high; the regression only bites when *every* candidate is no-quota on the current key. The same pattern already shipped for OCR, so this PR extends it rather than introducing it, but it is now the behaviour of every AI tool. It would be high if a free-tier key commonly returned `limit: 0` for Flash as well as Pro; the live-run evidence in the tech-debt register says it does not.
findings.summary: no-quota errors no longer fall through to API-key rotation

findings.detail: The `try` at :287 wraps the AI call *and* all of the post-processing — `alignBatchResults`, the `translationMap.set` loop, `addLog`, `setProgress`. Every error in that span is now run through `readableAiError`, so a `TypeError` from the alignment/apply code surfaces to the user as "The AI request failed unexpectedly" and is written into the PARTIAL workbook's "Stopped because" line under that wording. Before the change the real message was passed through. This is exactly the failure mode the same PR deliberately avoids in WebScraperTab.tsx:194-207 and documents in the comment there, so the two tabs now disagree on the rule. Low rather than medium because the post-AI code is pure and index-safe, and `readableAiError` still console.errors the original, so debuggability survives.
findings.summary: Translator's batch catch relabels its own errors as AI errors

findings.detail: `let result: any[];` is a new bare `any[]` in the diff with no justification comment, which is the shape `handbooks/language/typescript/type-safety.md` flags. Noting it for completeness rather than as a request: `IAiService.extractStructuredData` is already declared `Promise<any[]>` (types/ai.types.ts:71), so the annotation introduces no looseness that was not already there, and the hoisted `let` is required by the new try/catch. The actionable fix is at the interface, not here.
findings.summary: New `any[]` annotation, though it only mirrors the service's declared type
